paper.title: Partial Structure Discovery is Sufficient for No-regret Learning in Causal Bandits

settings.name_in_paper: Causal bandits with unknown causal graph containing latent confounders
unmapped: Arms are hard interventions do(W=w) on subsets of n discrete variables with domain size K_dom; (K_dom+1)^n arms
Unknown semi-Markovian causal graph with latent confounders; all observed variables are observed after each intervention
Interventional faithfulness and gap assumptions (epsilon for ancestrality, gamma for latent confounders, eta lower bound on nonzero interventional probabilities)
The learner knows the gap constants epsilon, gamma, eta, the max degree bound d_max, the number of nodes n and domain size K_dom
settings.definition_quote: We consider the causal bandit setup where all the observed variables $V_i \in \mathbf{V}$ are discrete with the domain $\Omega(V_i) = [K]$, and the reward $Y$ is binary ... an arm or action corresponds to hard intervention on a subset of variables other than the reward.

settings.name_in_paper: Finite-sample causal discovery with latent confounders via interventions
settings.out_of_scope_reason: Causal structure learning (graph discovery) from interventional samples, not a bandit regret/identification objective over arms.
unmapped: Goal is to learn the causal graph (observable edges and bidirected edges) w.p. >= 1-delta
Discrete variables with domain size K_dom; gap assumptions epsilon, gamma, eta known to learner; d_max >= max degree
settings.definition_quote: We propose a randomized algorithm for sample-efficient learning of causal graphs with confounders. We analyze the algorithm and bound the maximum number of interventional samples required to learn the causal graph with all the confounders with a given confidence level.

algorithms.name: Algorithm 3/6: two-phase causal bandit (partial discovery of POMISs + UCB)

bound.regime: on the event (probability >= 1-2*delta) that the POMIS set is learned correctly

symbols.K_dom: domain size of each discrete variable
symbols.n: number of observed nodes in the causal graph
symbols.eta_lb: lower bound on nonzero interventional probabilities (Assumption 4)
symbols.d_max: upper bound on max degree given to the algorithm
symbols.n_An: |An(Y)|, number of ancestors of the reward

tuning: delta_2 = delta_3 = delta_4 = delta/(64 alpha d_max log|An(Y)|)

source.label: thm_reg
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{sketch_band} learns the true set of POMISs with probability at least $1-2\delta$. Under the event that it learns POMISs correctly, the cumulative regret is bounded as follows: R_T\leq Kn\max(\frac{8}{\epsilon^2},\frac{8}{\gamma^2})\log{\frac{4n^2K^{2}}{\delta}} + \frac{8}{\epsilon^2}\log{\frac{4nK^{2}}{\delta}} + 8\alpha d_{max}(KA|\mathsf{An}(Y)| + \max(B,C)) \log(|\mathsf{An}(Y)|) + \sum ...

results.notes: Regret defined via expected rewards, but the bound holds only on an event of probability >= 1-2delta, so recorded as high-probability regret. The UCB term is summed over all POMIS arms in the paper; recorded as sum over suboptimal arms (Delta=0 terms undefined). The paper's K is variable domain size, renamed K_dom. Discovery terms are worst-case over tests.

bound.regime: learns the true observable graph w.p. >= 1 - 1/n^(alpha/(2d_max)-2) - 8 alpha d_max log(n)(n delta_1 + delta_2); >= 1-delta with the stated tuning

tuning: delta_1 = delta/(32 alpha d_max n log n)
delta_2 = delta/(32 alpha d_max log n)

source.label: thm1
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{algobs1} learns the true observable graph with probability at least $1-\frac{1}{n^{\frac{\alpha}{2d_{max}}-2}}-8\alpha d_{max} \log(n) (n \delta_1+\delta_2)$ with $8\alpha d_{max} \log{n}(KAn+B)$ interventional samples. If we set ... then Algorithm \ref{algobs1} learns the true observable graph with probability at least of $1-\delta$.

results.notes: Number of interventional samples to learn observable graph structure.

bound.regime: learns the true causal graph with latents w.p. >= 1 - 2/n^(alpha/(2d_max)-2) - 8 alpha d_max log(n)(n delta_1 + delta_2+delta_3+delta_4); >= 1-delta with stated tuning

tuning: delta_1 = delta/(64 alpha d_max n log n)
delta_2 = delta_3 = delta_4 = delta/(64 alpha d_max log n)

source.label: Thm_com
source.quote: Algorithm \ref{alg_c} learns the true causal graph with latents with probability at least $1-\frac{2}{n^{\frac{\alpha}{2d_{max}}-2}}-8\alpha d_{max} \log(n) (n \delta_1+(\delta_2+\delta_3+\delta_4))$ with a maximum of $8\alpha d_{max} \log{n}(KAn+\max(B,C))$ interventional samples.

results.notes: Full causal discovery including all latent confounders.
